exact_statement: For all integers a>=1 and even m>=4, the one-shared-bit Boolean family F defined in REPORT.md has n=1+am coordinates, a connected GF(2) ANF interaction graph at the root, and I(F)=a[(m-1)/2+m*delta]+[1-(-2delta)^a]/2, delta=2^-m. On the actual selector-first stopping tree, the sum of 2I(D_v), even after every disjoint independent factor is removed optimally at every node, is T_factor=a*m*delta+delta*a(a-1)[3(m-2)/4+(4m-2)delta]. At every selected descendant B_v/Inf_v>=(m-1)/2. For any fixed finite K>=0 choosing m with (m-1)/2>K makes all selected nodes bad while T_factor/I tends to infinity as a grows. This rejects only the specified selector-first rule plus factor-removal repair. Revealing the shared bit z first instead gives B_z<=1<=8 Inf_z/3, hence zero K=4 internal bad-node bill, and retains explicit terminal references with costs <=4I(z=0) and <=2I(z=1). The fixed normalized root reference Q(A,R)=[Q0(R)+Q1(R)]/4 has complete CE=am+2-[(1+delta^a)/2]log2(1+4^a)<=8I(F)/3, including every root/branch/terminal/empty-sector cost. Universal adaptive C019 and full FEI remain open.
